preamble: Nasalization of the alveolar implosive: [ɗ] becomes the nasal [n]. This is the coronal counterpart of Vietic *ɓ > m: Proto-Vietic *ɗ gives Vietnamese n (nước 'water' beside Mường đác and North Central Vietnamese nác), while Kri keeps ɗ and most other Vietic languages have d. The 'five' etymon goes back to Proto-Mon-Khmer *p(ɗ)am, so its initial was probably a cluster before reaching Proto-Vietic *ɗam.

examples.to: Vietnamese nước, North Central Vietnamese nác
examples.note: Kri ɗaːk keeps the implosive, Mường đác.
Mường đằm, Arem dam keep a stop.

languageExamples.language: Middle Mon to Modern Mon (after a nasal)

examples.note: Only after a nasal: word-initial dʔ survives (Modern Mon dʔa:k 'water'). Plain nd instead gives l (Old Mon kindar > Modern Mon kalaw 'wife', Old Mon dinduʔ > Modern Mon daloʔ 'teach').
